hardware.gpu: ANGLE (NVIDIA, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 (0x00002584) Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11)

conditions: Two six-second samples after warmup. Same real Orda renderer, 22 animated enemies, five cameras, five different viewmodels, same camera sweep, same framebuffer1669x939 at1920x1080 window. Fixed presentation fixture; no AI/network/full combat simulation.
graphics: Sharper concrete seams, grain and wear; cooler ambient fill with warmer directional light.
Shared baked-style contact shading under cover, soft instanced contact shadows for27 actors, warm floor light pools, cyan/amber wall guides. No extra dynamic lights or shadow maps.
Smaller premium station plates and compact translucent HUD; bounded boss bar.

Bacteria body uses one wet organic material instead of many near-black materials. Every original vertex and all three head/arm pivots retained; four meshes per actor. Other monster shapes and skins retained.
optimizations: Batched rigid Bacteria parts by material/layout:952 to652 average draws per frame.
Static monster and station materials frozen; unused pointer picking disabled; no preserved framebuffer copy.
Actor contact shadows use one instanced draw per camera rather than one draw per creature.

tests.verticesAndPivots: 15648 source vertices retained per Bacteria actor; Head/LeftArm/RightArm preserved

limits: One short before/after renderer comparison on RTX3050; not a long-session or full multiplayer FPS guarantee.
Final actor shadows consume about one draw per camera; final result39.2FPS supersedes an intermediate41.8FPS sample.
Scope is Orda; other minigames, shared gameplay rules and original Downloads assets were not changed.
